chapters.fx: What to watch: PPI (fcst 0.6% m/m, core 0.3%) + retail sales (fcst 0.3%) + claims (fcst 199K) Thursday 7:30am CT — the last hard data before the Oct 17 blackout. Hammack speaks 3:30pm CT, Warsh 10:30pm CT — the last two Fed voices before Saturday's quiet period.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the overnight chorus talked the October hike back down. Bowman's 'I don't feel any urgency for taking further action at this point' and Daly's 'hikes likely but not urgent for October' knocked October 27–28 pricing from the post-CPI ~49% coin flip to ~31.6% (LSEG: ~75% chance of a hold). DXY faded from the 102.75 18-month high to ~102.06; the 10-year fell to a three-week low of 5.1267%. Thread: yesterday's edition said hot core (0.3% m/m, 2.6% y/y — beats on both measures) broke the October-hold thesis and revived October to a coin flip, with December effectively fully priced. What it means: breaks yesterday's afternoon verdict — the October revival is now conditional, not a coin flip. The market's read (ANZ's Khoon Goh: the print was 'not hot enough to force the Fed's hand for October') is that one hot CPI doesn't buy the meeting two weeks out — the Fed wants to see PPI and retail sales first. December (~90–94%; Citi flipped hawkish — 25bp in December, then hold, no cuts until June 2027) is untouched: the overnight fade is about timing, not the path.
numbers: December ~90–94% (Citi: 25bp in Dec, then hold, no cuts to Jun 2027)
10Y 3-wk low 5.1267%; 2Y 4.80% — the CPI spike is unwinding

chapters.meaning: What changed: Washington weighed easing sanctions on shadow-fleet vessels (carrying Russian, Iranian and Venezuelan oil) to free 'legal oil' flows and ease record freight costs — a consideration, not an action yet — and it knocked ~$1.40 off Brent overnight. The API's huge -11.1M-barrel draw (Hurricane Isaias took ~two-thirds of Gulf Coast output offline) barely registered — Haitong noted buyers were unwilling to chase at $104+. Trump extended the Hormuz ultimatum to Saturday evening Oct 17: reopen the strait or the US hits Iranian power plants 'starting with the biggest one first'; Tehran denies talks are happening. The IEA's lid: Gulf producers' exports rose +4.4M bpd in September to ~75% of prewar levels. Thread: Monday bought the war back, Tuesday faded on diesel, Wednesday the Aramco/Hormuz confirmations re-bid, overnight the sanctions-easing talk leaked it again. What it means: confirms the range thesis — Brent $104–108 holds until a verified shock or ceasefire breaks it. The spread (~$10.5) says the premium is still shipping risk, not demand.
numbers: Trump Hormuz deadline: Saturday evening Oct 17

scenarios.base: Brent holds $104–108; the market needs a verified shock or ceasefire to leave the range.

scenarios.bull: Verified Hormuz disruption or a Saturday-deadline strike — Brent toward $110+, spread past $15.
